question: Stock JKL is making new highs while the consensus EPS estimate has been cut for several months. What is the most appropriate fusion-analysis conclusion?
options: Both disciplines agree, because price leads earnings and the market is looking through the cuts, so add to the position
Sell short immediately, because downward estimate revisions reliably lead price lower within weeks
The disciplines disagree, so conviction is lower; hold with tighter stops and let a break of trend confirm the warning
Disregard the revisions, since a new closing high means the technical evidence now outweighs them

question: Both stocks reported the same positive earnings surprise and briefly traded above resistance. Which offers the stronger fusion (fundamental + technical) long set-up?
options: ABC: the surprise is confirmed by a sustained breakout; DEF's failure after good news is a warning
DEF: the pullback after good news offers a cheaper entry into the same improved fundamental story
They are equally attractive, since both had the same surprise and both broke above resistance
DEF: a breakout that fails after good news is a bullish shakeout that usually precedes a stronger advance
concept: Earnings catalyst confirmed vs failed breakout

question: A fusion analyst will overweight Sector GHI only when its relative strength has broken above resistance AND upgrades outnumber downgrades. At which marked point are both conditions first met?
options: A
C
B
D
concept: Sector RS breakout plus improving revisions

question: Stock MNO's rally has come entirely from P/E expansion while earnings have been flat. Which response best reflects a fusion approach for a current holder?
options: Sell short now, because a P/E this far above its long-run average signals that a major top is imminent
Add to the position, because the expanding P/E confirms that earnings growth is about to accelerate
Close the position now and re-enter only after the P/E has reverted to its 18× ten-year average
Accept the valuation risk but let the trend time the exit: stay long until a technical breakdown
concept: Valuation is a poor timing tool; technicals time it

question: A fundamental screen flags Stock PQR as undervalued at the latest bar. What would a fusion analyst do?
options: Watch-list it and wait for technical evidence of a trend change, such as a sustained close above the 200-day average
Buy now, because a P/E well below the sector average limits downside risk regardless of the price trend
Buy half now and average down on further weakness, lowering the cost basis toward fair value
Sell short, because the falling P/E confirms that the company's fundamentals are deteriorating
concept: Fundamentals select, technicals time the entry
